negative_findings.description: No banking/payments-specific salary or hiring report published by a recruiter for Hungary was found. Finance appears only as a chapter or sector cut inside general HU salary guides (Hays) or general employment surveys (Manpower MEOS).

It also means no HU recruiter currently publishes payments-specific (PSP, acquiring, card-scheme) role data — a genuine market data void.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The seed query implied Trenkwalder as a finance labour-market source. It should be reclassified as macro labour-cost context, and the collection budget reallocated to Hays, Manpower MEOS and the executive-search mandate boards.

coverage_gaps.description: No HR-consultancy (as opposed to recruitment-agency) labour-market analysts were captured — e.g. the Big Four HR advisory practices, RSM Hungary (whose middle-manager salary analysis surfaced incidentally in Trenkwalder coverage), or academic/KSH labour analysts covering financial-services employment.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a pass on RSM Hungary's middle-management salary survey, Big Four HU reward-consulting publications, and KSH sector employment statistics for NACE K (financial and insurance activities) as the authoritative counterweight to recruiter self-report.

coverage_gaps.description: The two most complete structured datasets in this cell — the BBJ Book of Lists rankings and full recruiter salary-guide PDFs — are paywalled or lead-capture gated, and no fetch verification of any URL was performed in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for a BBJ Book of Lists purchase; register once per recruiter for guide downloads; run the deterministic liveness pass over every URL in this slice before relying on it.

coverage_gaps.description: Only current editions were located; historical archives of Hays HU salary guides and Manpower MEOS HU finance-sector readings were not enumerated, so no back-series exists yet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest prior-year editions via each publisher's archive and the Internet Archive to build a multi-year finance-sector hiring-intent and salary-band series.

brief: Hungary's recruiter/HR-analyst layer produces exactly two kinds of tractable evidence for banking and payments hiring: annual cross-sector salary guides with a finance chapter (Hays Hungary is the anchor, with a full 2026 PDF mirrored ungated on Pénzcentrum; Enloyd, Grafton and Randstad's benchmarking products are secondary), and a quarterly quantified hiring-intent series (ManpowerGroup's Munkaerőpiaci Előrejelzés, which breaks out 'pénzügy és biztosítás' as its own net-employment reading). No HU recruiter publishes a banking- or payments-specific report, so the finance signal must always be extracted as a sub-slice. The executive-search layer — Amrop Kohlmann & Young, HumanField, Beck & Partners, Stanton Chase, Horton International — is the indirect channel that reveals which institutions are staffing senior roles, and it is best enumerated through the pointer sources HR Portál, hrpwr.hu and the paid BBJ Book of Lists ranking rather than firm by firm. Two named actors in the cell brief did not hold up: Michael Page has no Hungarian office (CEE is run from Vienna) and Boyden produced no Hungarian footprint at all, while Trenkwalder's recurring product turns out to be a blue-collar hourly-wage barometer and belongs in macro context rather than financial-services coverage.
